To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The generalization performance of CNNs is not a function of the network depth, but it is a function of the size of the training set, and of the number of parameters of the network.

(a) CNNs with more layers generalize better than CNNs with less layers, (b) the training set needs to be sufficiently large for CNNs with more than 3 layers to generalize, (c) training set needs to have sufficient variability to allow CNNs to learn, and (d) CNNs with 3 or less layers are able to generalize even with small training sets, as long as the training set contains enough variability
“The generalization performance of a CNN depends on the training distribution and the CNN depth.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
How many training examples are needed to train a deep CNN? What is the impact of the CNN depth on the number of training examples needed?

two aspects of the problem of gender prediction: 1) the size of the training set required to achieve a certain performance level; and 2) the effect of the depth of the convolutional architecture on the final performance.
the question: how deep should a CNN be to guarantee generalization?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the generalization performance of CNNs increases with the depth.
the more complex the model, the more training data it needs to learn the underlying function.
, for binary classification, the more convolutional layers a CNN has the more data is required to train it, but the better it will generalize.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to guarantee a good generalization performance, the training set size should be proportional to the depth of the network, and that the network depth should be as small as possible, while maintaining a good classification accuracy.
, for a given problem, there is a minimum number of training examples that guarantees a certain generalization performance.
the size of the training data is a key ingredient to the generalization performance of a CNN, and that the CNN depth has to be carefully tuned to the training data size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CNNs can generalize well to unseen examples, even when trained with a small number of samples, provided that the CNN is not too deep.
the CNN depth does not necessarily improve the generalization performance of the classifier, but rather depends on the distribution and size of the training set.
, while the size of a CNN is crucial for its generalization ability, the training set size is not.
